title: dedicated-autoscaler: stabilize burst controls and improve utilization reporting
author: Priya Kaur
description: Motivation: Customers running Redwood Dedicated hit intermittent latency spikes when the fleet autoscaler applied burst capacity in high-churn workloads. Investigations showed race conditions in the token-bucket burst allocator and gaps in how burst events were annotated in fleet utilization reports. This PR stabilizes burst controls, smooths token-bucket transitions, and enriches utilization reporting so SREs and customers can reason about autoscale behavior. Changes: 1) Add a smoothing window to token-bucket refill to avoid large instantaneous token grants when many nodes join; 2) Serialize burst-apply operations in the autoscaler controller to prevent simultaneous double-allocation; 3) Emit structured burst events (start/stop/scale-reason) into the utilization reporting pipeline and add per-fleet burst_capacity and burst_in_flight metrics; 4) Improve rollout safety by adding a conservative default burst_limit_multiplier and a feature flag to opt-in to aggressive burst behavior; 5) Add unit and integration tests that simulate node churn and sustained enqueue pressure. Backwards compatibility: All changes are guarded by a feature flag (autoscaler.burst.smoothing.enabled=true) and default to conservative behavior to avoid customer impact. Testing: Local unit tests + integration test harness in perf-canary simulated 30-minute node churn scenario. Results: reduced observed burst-induced latency spikes by ~55% in the simulation and improved stability of reported utilization by removing duplicated burst annotations. Checklist: - [x] Implement smoothing logic in token-bucket refiller - [x] Add controller serialization around burst apply path - [x] Add metrics and event annotations for burst lifecycle - [x] Add integration tests and perf-canary scenario - [x] Add docs/CHANGELOG entries - [x] Feature-flagged rollout plan
commit_messages: tokenbucket: add smoothing window to refill to reduce burst spikes
autoscaler: serialize burst apply flow to avoid race conditions
reporting: emit burst_start/burst_stop events with scale_reason tags
metrics: add fleet.burst_capacity and fleet.burst_in_flight gauges
tests: add integration scenario for node churn and sustained enqueue pressure
docs: describe burst smoothing and rollout plan in autoscaler docs
review_comments: Evan Miller: Can we tighten the locking granularity so we don't serialise unrelated scale operations?
Lina Zhang: Add a metric for token refill rate so we can alert anomalous refill bursts.
Marco Alvarez: Integration test is great but can we extend it to include cross-region failover?
author_responses: Priya Kaur: Re: locking granularity - switched to per-fleet serialization instead of global, added a comment and unit test to validate concurrent unrelated ops are not blocked.
Priya Kaur: Added tokenbucket.refill_rate metric and a dashboard link in the docs.
Priya Kaur: Cross-region scenario is tracked in ENG-1299; will follow up in a follow-up PR to avoid scope creep for this stabilization.
release_notes: Stabilized autoscaler burst behavior by adding token-bucket smoothing and safer burst apply serialization. Added burst lifecycle events and new fleet-level metrics for better utilization reporting. Default conservative settings minimize customer impact; feature flag available for aggressive burst mode.
